prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the failure was never surfaced to the caller waiting on the associated request — it just returns/logs and the caller hangs forever ('infinite reconnection loop'). Both PRs target this exact branch in _handle_reconnection, just via different mechanisms: #2395 builds a JSONRPCError and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer so only the specific pending request gets failed while the session stays alive; #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError (via a new _unwrap_exception helper that digs the typed error out of anyio's ExceptionGroup wrapping) so the failure propagates as an exception out of the task group. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 edits the exact failure branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS) with a minimal, targeted change: it fails only the specific in-flight request with a proper JSONRPCError carrying the original request id, leaving the session and other in-flight requests unaffected. prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing relied on naive substring/regex matching for auth-params, which could false-positive on parameter values containing comma- or scheme-like substrings. Both replace it with a proper tokenizer that walks the header character-by-character, tracking quoted-string state and backslash escapes, splitting only on top-level (unquoted) commas. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing relied on naive substring/regex matching for auth-params, which could false-positive on parameter values containing comma- or scheme-like substrings. Both replace it with a proper tokenizer that walks the header character-by-character, tracking quoted-string state and backslash escapes, splitting only on top-level (unquoted) commas. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041's parser splits the WHOLE header into comma-separated segments first, then scans for a segment whose scheme token is 'Bearer' before collecting its auth-params — so it correctly isolates one challenge when a WWW-Authenticate header advertises multiple schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'), a case explicitly allowed by RFC 7235. PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead finds only the first space in the entire header and treats everything after it as one challenge's params, which breaks if the header contains more than one challenge/scheme. #3041 is also the larger, more complete diff (adds two cooperating helpers vs. one), reflecting this extra scheme-isolation logic.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both change the fixed 0-capacity (rendezvous) memory object stream used for stdio_server's write_stream, which forces the writer task to block until a reader is ready. #2215 makes the buffer size a caller-configurable parameter (default stays 0, so behavior is unchanged unless a caller opts in), while #2654 directly raises the write_stream default capacity to 1 so a handler can queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) without the caller having to do anything. #2654 fixes the blocking/ordering problem out-of-the-box and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact scenario; #2215 only fixes it if downstream code is updated to pass a non-default buffer size, so it doesn't resolve the bug for existing callers.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 edits the exact failure branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS) with a minimal, targeted change: it fails only the specific in-flight request with a proper JSONRPCError carrying the original request id, leaving the session and other in-flight requests unaffected. It also removes the pre-existing '# pragma: no cover' on that branch, indicating the new code path is exercised by a test. #3098's diff only adds a generic exception-unwrapping helper and an unrelated __future__ import style revert; the actual call site that would raise/propagate StreamableHTTPError isn't shown, and its approach (raising out of the task group) is more likely to tear down the whole client session rather than fail just the affected request.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the failure was never surfaced to the caller waiting on the associated request — it just returns/logs and the caller hangs forever ('infinite reconnection loop'). Both PRs target this exact branch in _handle_reconnection, just via different mechanisms: #2395 builds a JSONRPCError and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer so only the specific pending request gets failed while the session stays alive; #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError (via a new _unwrap_exception helper that digs the typed error out of anyio's ExceptionGroup wrapping) so the failure propagates as an exception out of the task group. (2 PRs)

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the same conditional block in validate_tool_use_result_messages() that governs behavior when an assistant's tool_use content is not followed by any tool_result block in the next message — but they resolve it in opposite, mutually exclusive ways. #2962 adds `has_tool_results` to the guard so the ID-matching check (and thus any error) is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, per SEP-1577 which only requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use, not the reverse (regression test cites issue #2960). #3053 keeps the original guard and instead adds an explicit `raise ValueError(...)` for the same no-tool_results case, just with a clearer message — i.e. it still treats the case as invalid. These are not compatible fixes to merge together: one makes the case pass validation, the other makes it fail with a (better-worded) error. They also textually conflict on the same lines in src/mcp/server/validation.py. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's parser splits the WHOLE header into comma-separated segments first, then scans for a segment whose scheme token is 'Bearer' before collecting its auth-params — so it correctly isolates one challenge when a WWW-Authenticate header advertises multiple schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'), a case explicitly allowed by RFC 7235. PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead finds only the first space in the entire header and treats everything after it as one challenge's params, which breaks if the header contains more than one challenge/scheme. #3041 is also the larger, more complete diff (adds two cooperating helpers vs. one), reflecting this extra scheme-isolation logic.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both change the fixed 0-capacity (rendezvous) memory object stream used for stdio_server's write_stream, which forces the writer task to block until a reader is ready. #2215 makes the buffer size a caller-configurable parameter (default stays 0, so behavior is unchanged unless a caller opts in), while #2654 directly raises the write_stream default capacity to 1 so a handler can queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification) without the caller having to do anything. #2654 fixes the blocking/ordering problem out-of-the-box and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact scenario; #2215 only fixes it if downstream code is updated to pass a non-default buffer size, so it doesn't resolve the bug for existing callers.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 edits the exact failure branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS) with a minimal, targeted change: it fails only the specific in-flight request with a proper JSONRPCError carrying the original request id, leaving the session and other in-flight requests unaffected. It also removes the pre-existing '# pragma: no cover' on that branch, indicating the new code path is exercised by a test. #3098's diff only adds a generic exception-unwrapping helper and an unrelated __future__ import style revert; the actual call site that would raise/propagate StreamableHTTPError isn't shown, and its approach (raising out of the task group) is more likely to tear down the whole client session rather than fail just the affected request.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the failure was never surfaced to the caller waiting on the associated request — it just returns/logs and the caller hangs forever ('infinite reconnection loop'). Both PRs target this exact branch in _handle_reconnection, just via different mechanisms: #2395 builds a JSONRPCError and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer so only the specific pending request gets failed while the session stays alive; #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError (via a new _unwrap_exception helper that digs the typed error out of anyio's ExceptionGroup wrapping) so the failure propagates as an exception out of the task group. (2 PRs)

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the same conditional block in validate_tool_use_result_messages() that governs behavior when an assistant's tool_use content is not followed by any tool_result block in the next message — but they resolve it in opposite, mutually exclusive ways. #2962 adds `has_tool_results` to the guard so the ID-matching check (and thus any error) is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, per SEP-1577 which only requires tool_result to be preceded by tool_use, not the reverse (regression test cites issue #2960). #3053 keeps the original guard and instead adds an explicit `raise ValueError(...)` for the same no-tool_results case, just with a clearer message — i.e. it still treats the case as invalid. These are not compatible fixes to merge together: one makes the case pass validation, the other makes it fail with a (better-worded) error. They also textually conflict on the same lines in src/mcp/server/validation.py. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's parser splits the WHOLE header into comma-separated segments first, then scans for a segment whose scheme token is 'Bearer' before collecting its auth-params — so it correctly isolates one challenge when a WWW-Authenticate header advertises multiple schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'), a case explicitly allowed by RFC 7235. PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead finds only the first space in the entire header and treats everything after it as one challenge's params, which breaks if the header contains more than one challenge/scheme. #3041 is also the larger, more complete diff (adds two cooperating helpers vs. one), reflecting this extra scheme-isolation logic.
